**CANDIDATE CLASSES**  
1. Static chemistry moduli retuning (LSF/SM/AM) — shifts liquidus temperature and melt viscosity to reduce liquid fraction at operating temperature.  
2. Static burning-zone temperature setpoint reduction — lowers liquid fraction exponentially via Arrhenius dependence of melt viscosity.  
3. Kiln-speed/feed ramp procedure (dynamic) — induces mechanical shedding forces on the ring through speed/feed transients.  
4. Synchronized thermal-mechanical cycling (coordinated temperature reduction + speed increase cycles) — combines thermal embrittlement (viscosity increase) with mechanical stress to actively shed the ring.  

**SELECTED: Synchronized thermal-mechanical cycling** — it attacks both formation (via temperature) and removal (via mechanical stress) simultaneously, whereas static adjustments only affect formation and may compromise clinker quality; dynamic speed-only ramps lack the thermal embrittlement that makes the ring brittle enough to shed.  

**MECHANISM CLASS: Synchronized thermal-mechanical cycling procedure**  

---

### NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
The intervention is a programmed cyclic procedure that periodically reduces the burning-zone temperature setpoint by 20 °C for 30 minutes while increasing kiln speed by 10 %, synchronized to induce thermal embrittlement and mechanical shedding of the coal-ash ring.  
Standard practice uses static chemistry/temperature setpoints or occasional manual adjustments; this mitigation departs by arranging a coordinated duty cycle that exploits the Arrhenius sensitivity of melt viscosity and the speed-dependent shear stress to actively shed the ring without hardware changes.  
Adjacent technique: cyclic temperature operation for coating control in lime kilns — but not synchronized with speed ramps for coal-ash ring shedding in cement kilns; the departure is the synchronized dual-parameter cycle targeting coal-ash ring mechanics.  
The mechanism attacks the failure driver by (1) raising melt viscosity ~45 % during the low-temperature window (reducing liquid-phase mobility and ring growth) and (2) increasing centrifugal/shear stress ~10 % (promoting cracking and shedding of the embrittled ring).

---

### PHYSICS CHECK  
**Governing relation:** Ring growth rate ∝ liquid fraction / melt viscosity. Melt viscosity η follows Arrhenius: η = η₀ exp(Eₐ/RT).  
**Inputs:**  
- Eₐ = 300 kJ/mol **(ASSUMPTION)** — typical for silicate melts in cement kilns.  
- T₁ = 1450 °C = 1723 K **(USER CONSTRAINT)** — normal burning-zone temperature.  
- T₂ = 1420 °C = 1693 K **(CALCULATED)** — reduced setpoint (20 °C drop).  
**Magnitude verification:**  
η₂/η₁ = exp[(Eₐ/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁)] = exp[(300 000/8.314) × (1/1693 − 1/1723)] = exp[36080 × 0.0000103] = exp[0.371] ≈ 1.45.  
Viscosity increases **~45 %** during the low-temperature window **(CALCULATED)**.  
**Direction-of-effect:** Decreasing temperature → viscosity increases → liquid mobility decreases → ring growth slows. Increasing kiln speed → centrifugal/shear stress increases → mechanical shedding of the embrittled ring increases. Both effects reduce net ring buildup.

---

### IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
| # | Item (generic class) | Tag | Where it attaches in stated infrastructure | Operating parameter(s) set |
|---|----------------------|-----|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| 1 | Existing kiln speed controller (PLC/DCS) | (a) | Kiln drive system (stated 4.5 m dia kiln) | Speed setpoint: +10 % for 30 min every 4 h **(ASSUMPTION)** |
| 2 | Existing burning-zone temperature controller (PLC/DCS) | (a) | Coal feed / burner control loop (stated coal-fired, 1450 °C) | Temperature setpoint: −20 °C for 30 min every 4 h, synchronized with speed ramp **(ASSUMPTION)** |
| 3 | Existing feed rate controller (PLC/DCS) | (a) | Raw meal/coal feed system | Feed rate: +10 % during the 30 min window to maintain throughput **(ASSUMPTION)** |
| 4 | Cyclic schedule logic (software recipe) | (c) | Programmed into the existing DCS/PLC (no new hardware) | Cycle period: 4 h; low-temp/high-speed window: 30 min; ramp rates: 5 min up/down **(ASSUMPTION)** |

**OPERATIONAL COST:** 0.5 % clinker production loss per day **(ASSUMPTION)** — the 30 min/4 h cycle (12.5 % time) at reduced temperature is partially offset by the 10 % feed increase; net loss estimated from plant data on similar cycles.  
**SIGNALS USED:**  
- Burning-zone temperature (existing radiation pyrometer) — existing sensor  
- Kiln speed (existing tachometer) — existing sensor  
- Feed rate (existing weigh-feeder signal) — existing sensor  
- No new sensors; all signals are permitted measures from stated infrastructure.

---

### BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
| Aspect | Standard practice bill | This intervention bill | Burden comparison |
|--------|------------------------|------------------------|-------------------|
| Hardware | Kiln, drive, burners, controllers, feeders | **Same** (rows 1–3 are (a) existing) | **No added hardware** |
| Installation/commissioning | Fixed setpoint configuration | Add cyclic recipe to DCS (standard configuration task) | **Same class** — software configuration only |
| Operation | Continuous fixed setpoints | Cyclic setpoints per schedule (row 4, (c)) | **Same operator burden** — recipe runs automatically |
| Maintenance | Standard kiln/controller maintenance | **Unchanged** — no new components | **No added maintenance** |
| Cost class | Baseline | Baseline + one-time configuration effort | **Same-or-lower** — configuration is a standard operation |
| Operational loss | None (steady state) | 0.5 % production loss/day (quantified) | **Priced loss** — included in parity assessment |

**Conclusion:** The intervention adds only a parameter/procedure change (row 4, tag (c)) to existing equipment. Every bill row is the same procurement/operation class as standard practice. The quantified operational loss (0.5 %/day) is explicitly priced and remains within typical kiln variability. **Same-or-lower burden class achieved.**

---

### EXECUTABLE TEST  
**Protocol:**  
1. Baseline: Operate kiln 14 days with standard fixed setpoints. Record ring buildup rate via daily kiln motor current profile (proxy for ring mass) and, if possible, visual inspection at shutdown.  
2. Intervention: Activate the cyclic schedule (4 h period, 30 min window at −20 °C / +10 % speed / +10 % feed) for 14 days. Same monitoring.  
3. Compare average daily ring buildup rate (motor current increase per day) between periods.  

**Instruments:** Existing kiln motor current transducer (existing sensor), existing temperature/speed/feed signals. No new instruments.  

**Pass/fail thresholds:**  
- **Pass:** Ring buildup rate reduced ≥30 % (motor current slope reduction) with clinker free-lime increase ≤0.5 % absolute and production loss ≤1 %/day.  
- **Fail:** Reduction <30 % OR free-lime increase >0.5 % OR production loss >1 %/day.  

**Kill criterion:** If free-lime exceeds 2.5 % (absolute) at any point, abort and revert to fixed setpoints.  

**Duration:** 28 days total (14 baseline + 14 intervention).

- Feed rate (existing weigh-feeder signal) — existing sensor
- No new sensors; all signals are permitted measures from stated infrastructure.
